resources.string: 1. Camera: Wi-Fi → MobileLink (camera\'s own Wi-Fi) or Samsung Link → Nearby devices (same Wi-Fi as the phone).\n2. Phone: join the camera\'s network and keep it.\n3. Tap Find camera. If the camera asks whether to allow this phone, choose Allow / OK.
Keep the phone on the camera\'s Wi-Fi network.
%1$s · %2$s\nTap a photo to select or deselect it, then tap Download.
Connect to the camera, then tap Find camera.
Files are in Pictures/CamLink and Movies/CamLink.
The gateway shown in the phone\'s Wi-Fi details. MobileLink cameras are often 192.168.101.1. You can add a port if the camera uses one.
That does not look like an address. Try 192.168.1.1.
Looking at Wi-Fi, SSDP, the device description and camera web pages. This can take up to a minute.

CamLink talks to Samsung Wi-Fi cameras over standard DLNA/UPnP, the same protocol the camera already exposes for Samsung Link and Mobile Link.

It never writes to the camera and never deletes anything. Downloads go to Pictures/CamLink (photos) and Movies/CamLink (videos).

Built for the WB1100F, but works with any Samsung camera that publishes a ContentDirectory service.

No camera found on this network.\n\nCheck that the phone is joined to the camera\'s Wi-Fi and the camera is in MobileLink or Samsung Link (Nearby devices) mode. If it still fails, open the menu and tap Diagnose connection, then share the report.

The camera refused access (HTTP 401).

CamLink sent the same pairing request the Samsung app uses. Look at the camera screen: if it asks whether to allow this phone, choose Allow / OK.

MobileLink: stay on the MobileLink screen, then tap Find camera again.
Samsung Link: press Menu → DLNA Access Control → All devices.
Could not reach a camera at %1$s.\n\nCheck the address and that the phone is on the camera\'s Wi-Fi network.
Found %1$s, but it has no ContentDirectory service. Send the connection details from the menu so the protocol can be checked.
